svg.title: A stable prefix turns into a cache hit
svg.desc: Two hand-drawn token bars of identical width, one above the other. The first, labelled call one and cold, splits into a 4,600-token stable segment of system prompt and tools and a 5,900-token volatile segment of user turn and history; the whole 10,500 tokens bill at full rate. An arrow leads down to a dashed box marked KV-cache stored, with about a five minute idle lifetime, holding the keys and values already computed for the prefix. A second arrow leads to the warm call, whose prefix segment occupies exactly the same width but is now a cache hit billed at roughly a tenth of the input rate, while the volatile segment still pays full rate. A caption states that a cache breakpoint is a prefix match from the first byte, and that any change invalidates the cache from that point to the end.
svg.text: Prompt caching: same prefix, new suffix
A prefix that does not change byte-for-byte is stored once and replayed at about a tenth of the input rate.
The provider keeps the keys and values it already
computed for the prefix, keyed by the exact byte
A cache breakpoint is a prefix match measured from the very first byte.
Any change invalidates the cache from the point of change to the end of the request.
